div.head: III Atr 1
div.ab: Ðæt is: þæt his grið stande swa forð, swa hit fyrmest stód on his yldrena dagum, þæt þæt sy bótléas, þæt he mid his agenre hánd sylð.
Id est, ut pax eius firma sit, sicut prius extitit in diebus antecessorum suorum, et preter emendationem sit infractio pacis, quam per manum suam dabit.
Ðæt is: þæt his grið stande swa forð swa hit fyrmest stód on his yldrena dagum, þæt þæt sy bótléas þæt he mid his agenre hánd sylð.

Nämlich, dass Sonderschutz von ihm [verliehen] so weiter fortbestehe, wie er bestens bestand in seiner Vorfahren Tagen: dass der, welchen er mit seiner eigenen Hand giebt, [wenn gebrochen, durch Geld] unabbüssbar sei.
Namely, that the special protection [granted] by him continue as it stood at its best in the days of his ancestors: that what he gives with his own hand be [if broken] beyond compensation [by money].

Namely, that the king's peace shall continue to be maintained in accordance with the highest standards observed in the days of his ancestors, so that breach of the peace which he establishes in person shall not be atoned for by any payment of compensation.
Namely, in order that his peace may remain as firm as it best was in the days of his ancestors, [breach of] that peace which he gives with his own hand is not to be atoned for by compensation.

note.seg: Königsfriede (s. d. Gl) samt Strafgeld für dessen Bruch, dem sog. ‘Königsschutz’ (s. d. Gl), gilt also trotz Nord. Namens richtig als eine Agsä., bis vor Mitte 10. Jhs. hinaufgehende Einrichtung

The king’s peace (see that word in Gl), together with the fine for its breach, the so-called ‘king’s protection’ (see that word in Gl), is thus rightly regarded, despite the Norse name, as an Anglo-Saxon institution going back to before the middle of the 10th cent.

firma entnimmt Q aus dem Klange von fyrmest, das Wort prius aus dessen anderer Bed. oder dem Zusammenhange. ‘Zuerst, ursprünglich’ verstehen Price-Thorpe, Schmid; allein Æthelred braucht das Wort sonst für ‘weitest, zumeist’ VI 40. X Pro. Weniger auf den Ursprung als die Ausdehnung der Prärogative kam es an.—Den höchsten Grad drückt auch sonst der ‘beste frühere Zustand’ aus; s. o. II Eg 5, 3¹

Q derives firma from the sound of fyrmest, and the word prius from its other meaning or from the context. ‘First, originally’ is how Price-Thorpe and Schmid understand it; but Æthelred elsewhere uses the word for ‘furthest, most’, VI 40. X Pro. What mattered was less the origin than the extent of the prerogative.—The highest degree is also expressed elsewhere by the ‘best former state’; see above II Eg 5, 3¹
Vgl. Gl Handfrieden 3a. 5Aa (emendari non po[test] Hn 12, 1a); busslos 1. 5
